title: Database Systems
description: Model facts precisely, execute and cost queries, then test data correctness under concurrency, failure, distribution, and hostile access.
overview: A DBMS is studied as a correctness-preserving execution engine. Learners map domain claims into constrained relations, predict query semantics and cost from visible tables and plans, trace schedules and recovery, and defend distributed and security trade-offs with evidence.

required: Sets, predicates, relations, and basic data structures
recommended: Asymptotic notation, trees, hashing, and basic probability
